title: Call QA and Compliance Auditing on Every Call
summary: Score every recorded call against your QA form and compliance script, in Hindi, Hinglish and English, so QA analysts spend their time on the calls that need a human ear.

seo.title: AI Call QA and Compliance Auditing | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that transcribes every call in Hindi, Hinglish and English, scores it against your QA form and compliance script, and routes breaches to QA analysts.

problem.intro: QA teams typically listen to a small, fixed sample of calls per agent each month and score them on a form covering opening, verification, hold etiquette, mandatory disclosures, resolution and closing. Breaches on unsampled calls, such as a skipped disclosure, a misleading promise or a rude exchange, surface only when a customer complains or a client audits the programme.

pain_points.title: Small sample coverage
pain_points.detail: A handful of calls per agent cannot show whether a disclosure is skipped routinely or only once.

pain_points.title: Inconsistent scoring
pain_points.detail: Two analysts score the same call differently, and calibration sessions take time away from listening.

pain_points.title: Code-mixed audio defeats keyword spotting
pain_points.detail: Legacy speech analytics built for English keywords misses Hinglish phrasing of the same disclosure or promise.

pain_points.title: Feedback arrives too late
pain_points.detail: Agents receive coaching weeks after the call, when they no longer remember it, and disputes are hard to settle without evidence.

solution.overview: We build a call QA pipeline that picks up recordings from your dialler or recording platform after each call, transcribes them with speaker separation and evaluates the conversation against your own QA form and compliance checklist. Each parameter is scored with the transcript excerpt that justifies it: whether the agent verified identity before discussing the account, read the mandatory disclosure, avoided prohibited promises, followed hold procedure and closed correctly. Compliance-critical failures and low-confidence scores go to QA analysts, who confirm or overturn them, and their decisions are used to calibrate the evaluator. Team leaders get agent-level trends and coaching clips instead of a monthly spreadsheet.
capabilities: Transcription with agent and customer separation for Hindi, Hinglish, English and agreed regional languages
Scoring against your QA form, parameter by parameter, with the quoted evidence behind each score
Compliance checks for mandatory disclosures, verification steps, prohibited phrases and promises
Detection of abusive language, escalation requests and dissatisfaction signals
Analyst review queue for critical failures and uncertain scores, with calibration tracking
Agent and team dashboards with coaching clips linked to the exact moment in the call

workflow.title: Ingest recordings
workflow.detail: Recordings and call metadata such as agent, campaign and disposition are collected after each call.

workflow.title: Transcribe and separate speakers
workflow.detail: Audio is transcribed with agent and customer labelled, and card numbers or OTPs are redacted.

workflow.title: Score against the QA form
workflow.detail: Each parameter is scored with the excerpt that supports it, and compliance rules are checked.

workflow.title: Review critical results
workflow.detail: Compliance-critical failures and low-confidence scores go to a QA analyst to confirm or overturn.

workflow.title: Log decisions for calibration
workflow.detail: Analyst decisions are recorded and used to tune the evaluator and track agreement.

workflow.title: Publish to team leaders
workflow.detail: Scores, trends and coaching clips appear on agent and team dashboards.

inputs: Call metadata such as agent ID, campaign and disposition
Compliance scripts and prohibited phrase lists
human_in_the_loop: QA analysts confirm every compliance-critical failure before it reaches an agent's scorecard or a client report, and they handle all agent disputes. Analyst decisions are tracked so the evaluator's agreement with humans stays visible.
integrations: Recording and dialler platforms such as Genesys, Avaya, NICE, Ozonetel or Exotel
BI tools such as Power BI
guardrails: No score without a quoted transcript excerpt
Compliance-critical failures confirmed by an analyst before they count
Card numbers and OTPs redacted from transcripts
Agent dispute path with recorded outcomes
Data separated by programme and client in multi-client BPOs
compliance_notes: Card details spoken on calls should be paused or redacted to support PCI DSS; the pipeline redacts card-like numbers from transcripts.
Recordings, transcripts and QA scores are personal data of customers and agents under the DPDP Act 2023.

pilot.scope: One programme or queue, using a few weeks of recordings, run in parallel with the existing manual QA.
deliverables: QA form and compliance checklist configured as a rubric
Scored calls for the pilot period

what_we_measure.how: Parameter-level comparison with analyst scores on the same calls.
Word error rate on sampled calls, by language and audio quality.
Compliance-critical failures on unsampled calls, as confirmed by analysts.
Time to confirm or overturn a flagged result, compared with full listening.

faqs.q: How accurate is automated scoring compared with our QA analysts?
faqs.a: We measure it parameter by parameter against your analysts' scores on the same calls during the pilot. Objective parameters such as verification and disclosures are easier to score consistently than subjective ones such as empathy, which is why compliance-critical failures always go to an analyst before they count.

faqs.q: Our recordings are mono and noisy. Will it work?
faqs.a: Stereo recordings with agent and customer on separate channels give the best results, but mono recordings work with speaker separation. The pilot reports transcription quality on your actual audio so you can see the effect before committing.
Hindi, Hinglish and English are the starting point. Regional languages are added based on your programmes and tested on your own recordings first.

faqs.q: Can agents see and dispute their scores?
faqs.a: Yes. Agents and team leaders see each score with the transcript excerpt and audio clip behind it, and disputes go to a QA analyst whose decision is recorded.
